what_its_for: Losartan is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It helps relax your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard to pump blood. It is also used to protect the kidneys in people with type 2 diabetes and to reduce the risk of stroke in people with high blood pressure and an enlarged heart.
how_to_take: Take losartan by mouth with or without food, usually once or twice a day. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time every day so it becomes part of your routine. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist says it is okay.
dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 50 mg once a day. Your doctor may adjust your dose anywhere from 25 mg to 100 mg per day depending on how well your blood pressure is controlled and how you respond to the medication. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store losartan at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid using potassium supplements or salt substitutes that contain potassium unless your doctor tells you it is okay, as losartan can raise your potassium levels. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and cause dizziness. Be careful when standing up quickly, especially in hot weather or after exercise, as you may feel lightheaded. Avoid taking NSAIDs (such as ibuprofen or naproxen) regularly without checking with your doctor, as they may reduce how well losartan works and can harm your kidneys. Do not take losartan if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can cause serious harm to an unborn baby.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (this could be a serious allergic reaction called angioedema); difficulty breathing or swallowing; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, or numbness; signs of kidney problems such as little or no urination, swelling in your legs or feet; severe dizziness or fainting; or if you become pregnant while taking this medication. Contact your doctor if you have ongoing diarrhea or vomiting, as this can affect your blood pressure and kidney function.
when_it_works: You may start to see a drop in your blood pressure within 1 week of starting losartan, but it may take up to 3 to 6 weeks to see the full benefit. Even if you feel well, keep taking your medication every day. High blood pressure often has no symptoms, so do not stop taking losartan without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take losartan if you are pregnant. It can cause serious injury or death to an unborn baby. Use effective birth control while taking this medication. If you become pregnant, call your doctor immediately. Breastfeeding: It is not known if losartan passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Losartan can be used in children 6 years of age and older with high blood pressure. The dose is based on the child's weight. Older adults (65+): Older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects of losartan and may be at higher risk for dizziness and falls. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may start you on a lower dose if you have liver problems. Tell your doctor about any kidney or liver conditions you have.
